title: The Belle Époque
subject: histoire
description: Between the end of the war of 1870 and August 1914, Europe believed in progress. Electricity, exhibitions, new arts… and fractures that lead to catastrophe.

hero.hook: Forty years of faith in progress… before everything changed in 1914.

blocks.text: The **Belle Époque** designates the period of relative peace between the end of the [[Franco-Prussian War]] (**1871**) and the start of the [[World War I]] (**1914**). We believe in science, in progress, in reason.
For the wealthy classes of Western Europe, it was four decades of comfort and invention. But beneath the veneer there already shine social fractures and rivalries that will blow everything up.

A second industrial revolution brings **electricity**, **oil**, chemistry. The tram and the metro (Paris, **1900**) are changing the city. The automobile and the plane are born. The telephone shortens distances.

blocks.caption: The 1900 Universal Exhibition in Paris, a showcase of progress.

blocks.text: The name “Belle Époque” only appears after **1914**. Contemporaries did not live in “the Belle Époque”: it was the survivors of the trenches who invented this lost paradise.

The **1900 World's Fair** attracts **50 million** visitors. The Lumière brothers' cinema and the Moulin Rouge make Paris a capital of entertainment. , a highly influential philosophy, sums up the optimism: science will solve everything. [[The positivism of Auguste Comte]]
Behind the boulevards, workers often work **10 to 12 hours** per day, without real protection. Urban poverty fuels tensions between classes.

blocks.caption: The Eiffel Tower (1889), icon of a modernity that does not benefit everyone.

blocks.text: On a global scale, Europe shares Africa. The [[The Berlin Conference (1884-1885)]] (**1884-1885**) sets borders without consulting the peoples concerned. In France, the [[Dreyfus Affair (1894-1906)]] tears the Republic apart: a Jewish officer, Alfred Dreyfus, is wrongly convicted of espionage, and anti-Semitism comes to light.

The arts are exploding. The [[Art Nouveau]] curves the facades. The [[Fauvism]] and shake up the paint. Doctor explores the unconscious. Albert Einstein publishes in **1905**: space and time are no longer what we thought. [[Cubism]] [[Sigmund Freud]] [[Relativity]]
In **1913**, the ballet *The Rite of Spring* by Igor Stravinsky caused such a scandal in Paris that spectators came to blows.

Then everything changes. On **June 28, 1914**, Archduke **Franz Ferdinand**, heir of Austria-Hungary, was assassinated in Sarajevo. The gears of alliances are set in motion. On **August 4**, the United Kingdom enters the war. Faith in progress dies in the trenches.

blocks.text: The Belle Époque (**1871-1914**) combines technical progress and deep fractures, before sinking into the chaos of the Great War.
